name: Famotidine
dosing: Peptic ulcer: commonly 40 mg nocte or 20 mg twice daily; GORD: 20–40 mg twice daily depending on severity; adjust dose in renal impairment
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to famotidine or related H2 antagonists
interactions: Fewer clinically significant interactions than cimetidine; may reduce absorption of azole antifungals (ketoconazole, itraconazole) due to altered gastric pH; overall interaction profile favourable
monitoring: Assess symptom response and healing where clinically indicated; check renal function and adjust dose in renal impairment
pregnancy: Use only if essential; avoid unnecessary exposure but may be used when clinically indicated
sideEffects: Common: headache, dizziness, gastrointestinal upset (nausea, constipation, diarrhoea); rare: confusion in elderly or those with severe renal impairment
pharmacokinetics: Oral administration with predominant renal excretion; dose adjustment required in renal impairment
clinicalPearls: Less interaction-prone than cimetidine; proton pump inhibitors are generally preferred for many acid-related conditions but famotidine is useful when PPIs are contraindicated or not tolerated
indication: Peptic ulcer disease, gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD), and symptomatic relief of dyspepsia
